texts.facts: ORDER Petitioners are traders carrying on various types of business including hotel business. They have filed these writ petitions seeking direction to the respondents to implement the directions issued by the Apex Court in the matter of MAHARASTRA EKTA HAWKERS` UNION Vs. MUNICIPAL CORPORATION, GREATER MUMBAI, reported in AIR 2004 SC 416. 2. The grievance of the petitioners is that, though the Apex Court has issued guidelines directing the appropriate Government to issue directions with regard to regulating the hawking business, so far, No.2 - Hubli Dharwad Municipal Corporation has not implemented the directions of the Apex Court. Petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Maharastra Ekta Hawkers` Union (referred supra) as well as the decision of the Division Bench of this Court in W.P. No.14607/2008 dated 04.12.2008, wherein this Court also having regard to the decision of the Apex Court has given direction to all the Municipal Corporations, including Hubli-Dharwad Municipal Corporation to take all necessary and appropriate steps to regulate the hawkers and the footpath shop vendors. 3. It is the case of the petitioners that, they are all traders trading in various businesses after obtaining licences and have invested money in establishing their permanent business and are incurring recurring expenditure towards rent, electricity, water, employment of labourers and tax etc. However, the act of the respondents allowing the hawkers to carry on their hawking business across the road or in places abutting their permanent establishments has vitally affected their business and thereby, it has denied their fundamental right guaranteed under Articles 19(1)(g) and 21 of the Constitution of India. Hence, they are before this Court to seek direction to the respondents. 4. During the pendency of these writ petitions, respondent No.2 - Municipal Corporation has filed status report inter alia stating that they have identified the hawking zone and have agreed to implement the directions issued by the Apex Court as well as the Division Bench of this Court. However, it was submitted that, the hawking zone demarcated would either affect the vehicular Sukumar S/O. Sanjeev Shetty vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 January, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25860667/ 7 movement or it will go contrary to the guidelines of the Hon`ble Supreme Court. Hawkers Association, which is before this Court, has filed an application for impleading in W.P. No.66400/2012 and their grievance is that the hawking zone has not been properly demarcated.
texts.arguments: 5. The Apex Court in the decision of MAHARASTRA EKTA HAWKERS` UNION has carved out 16 guidelines, which read as under: (i) an area of 1 mtr x 1 mtr on one side of the footpath wherever they exist or on an extreme side of the carriage way, in such a manner that the vehicular and pedestrian traffic is not obstructed and access to shops and residences is not blocked. (ii) Hawkers must not put up stalls or place any tables, stand or such other thing or erect any type of structure. (iii) There should be no hawking within 100 meters from any place of worship, holy shrine, educational institutions and hospitals or within 150 meters from any municipal or other markets or from any railway station. We direct that no cooking of any nature whatsoever shall be permitted. Sukumar S/O. Sanjeev Shetty vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 January, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25860667/ 8 However the payment of prescribed fee shall not be deemed to authorize the hawker to do his business beyond prescribed hours and would not confer on the hawker the right to do business at any particular place; (viii) The hawkers must extend full cooperation to the municipal conservancy staff for cleaning the streets and footpaths and also to the other municipal staff for carrying on any municipal work. The licence must be displayed, at all times, by the hawkers on their person by clipping it on to their shirt or coat; (xi) Not more than one member of a family must be given a licence to hawk. 9. The learned counsel appearing for the Municipal Corporation submits that, 7 hawking zones are identified in Dharwad and 21 hawking zones in Hubli City. In respect of hawkers, who are yet to obtain licence, learned counsel for the Corporation submitted that, they will issue appropriate paper publication for the awareness of the hawkers and give reasonable time to such hawkers to make application for grant of licence and permission. Similarly, for grant of licenses to the hawkers in respect of food articles under the Sukumar S/O. Sanjeev Shetty vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 January, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25860667/ 10 provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Regulation 2.1.1 of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Business) Regulations, 2011, (for short, `the Regulations`), stipulates that, every petty food business operator is required to register themselves with the Registering Authority. 12. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Corporation submits that, four months time may be granted for processing and issuing permission and within the said period, if the hawkers had applied for license under the regulation, such application would be disposed in four months time. 13. The learned counsel representing the hawkers Association would submit that, the hawkers would make necessary application for license under the regulation and for permission to Municipal Corporation by complying with all the requirements. 16. The Commissioner of the Corporation, who is before this Court submits that, as many as eight R.O. Water supply Centers are provided in Hubli and steps would be taken to provide R.O. water supply centers nearer to the hawking zone and also for general public at bare minimal rate as people, who cannot afford to have mineral water at the market rate can have benefit of quality drinking water at a cheaper rate. 17. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Corporation also submits that, all steps would be taken to prevent health hazards and all necessary facilities would be provided to hawkers depending on the category of vending done by them. He further submitted that, the process of completing the exercise of identifying hawking zones and regulating business of hawking and also providing facilities to the hawkers would take minimum eight months time as it involves the coordination with the other departments. In this regard, the learned counsel representing the second respondent - Corporation and the Additional Government Advocate representing the Commissioner of Police submit that, the District Surveillance officer, who is the designated officer / authority for issuing licences under the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011, will file necessary affidavit and all the three authorities submitted that, they will work in coordination and implement the guidelines of the Apex Court in letter and spirit within eight months.
